test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the most suitable idiom for the given situation.

Your friend has already told me everything about your secret surprise that you were planning for the last two weeks.

options.text: To keep something under your hat

solution:
The correct answer is '**To spill the beans**'. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**To spill the beans**" means to reveal a secret or disclose information that was supposed to be kept confidential.
 
• In the given situation, your friend has already disclosed the secret surprise that you were planning for the last two weeks. 
 
• This fits the context of revealing something that was meant to be kept secret, hence "**to spill the beans**" is the most appropriate idiom.
 
• It is clear from the above explanation that the correct answer is '**To spill the beans**'.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the meanings of other options.
 
• **To keep something under your hat:** This means to keep something secret or confidential. However, in this situation, the secret has already been revealed, so this idiom doesn't fit.
 
• **Behind closed doors: **This phrase means something done privately or secretly, away from public view. It doesn't directly relate to revealing a secret that was supposed to be kept confidential.

 
 
• 
 
**My lips are sealed: **This idiom means to promise not to reveal a secret. However, in this situation, the secret has already been disclosed by the friend, so it doesn't fit the context.
